Spikes correctly flag level 2 (Cosmic Binding beats double Power Chord), level 6 (Crescendo AoE stun), first item (aura sustain evens poke), late (dual-ult coin flip).

audit.whatIsWrong: full-layer phases[3/5/6].side (Skill, Sona, Sona) contradict content win[3/5/6] (Bard, Skill, Skill) and also contradict their own matchup's well-reasoned content whys, which argue Bard stays ahead through levels 4-5 and the poke war merely evens (not flips to Sona) at first item and late.
audit.why: phases[N].side and win[N] are the same row and must agree; the content layer's specific reasoning (stun-pick range advantage, Meeps auto-trade wins, aura sustain evening rather than reversing the poke, dual-ult late coinflip) is grounded in the kits and packet.defects itself flags the chart as suspect, so the generic full-layer side/why (which never argues a Sona lead) is the stale one.
audit.corrected: Moved phases[3].side to Bard, phases[5]/[6].side to Skill to match win[], and rewrote each why to state the specific reason instead of the generic template.

notes: packet.defects itself flags this chart as suspect (Bard's real winrate 47.32% vs a chart giving Bard 4/7 stages, 0 for Sona). Investigating showed the DISAGREEMENT was actually between the two layers, not a bad overall verdict: content win[]/whys[] (Bard,Bard,Bard,Bard,Skill,Skill,Skill) is detailed and kit-grounded (Cosmic Binding outranging Sona early, Crescendo evening at 6, aura items evening the poke at first item, dual-ult late coinflip), while full phases[3,5,6] carried generic filler why-text that never argued a Sona lead yet still flagged side=Sona. Moved full phases[3,5,6].side/rating to match win[] and replaced the generic whys with the specific reasoning already implied by content. This keeps the ~47% overall winrate plausible (early Bard edge nets out against a truly even mid/late) without inventing a Sona-favored late game the content never supports.
